purpose: Auditable CUAI process, reliability, measurement and operating-improvement backlog. Entries record evidence, bounded change, expected benefit, risk, validation, status, result and rollback.

entries.evidence: Multiple recent published articles referenced /assets/site.js, while the canonical article template references /assets/app.js. The production /assets/site.js path returned HTTP 404. assets/app.js contains the CUAI article_view, engaged_reader, scroll_depth, newsletter_intent, source_click and related_content_click logic, so affected pages retained basic inline GA4 page measurement but did not reliably execute the CUAI editorial event layer.
entries.proposedChange: Restore /assets/site.js as a backward-compatible loader for the canonical /assets/app.js bundle and make the analytics validator fail when a new article references a missing shared app/site script.
entries.expectedBenefit: Restore custom editorial measurement and shared article behavior on already-published pages without rewriting them, while preventing the same broken-asset class from passing future publication validation.
validation: node syntax checks passed for the compatibility loader and validator
Vercel preview reached READY
preview /assets/site.js returned HTTP 200 and loaded /assets/app.js
preview /assets/app.js returned HTTP 200
PR #131 diff was reviewed and mergeability verified
production deployment reached READY on commit 833bddc9cb0bc1b7555d5cb40da41c9566147edc
production /assets/site.js returned HTTP 200
GA4 and Buffer reporting endpoints remained HTTP 200/ok=true after deployment
entries.result: PR #131 merged. Historical overall GA4 traffic/acquisition remains usable, but CUAI custom article-event history on pages that referenced the missing script is quality-labeled as incomplete before the repair.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #131 or remove assets/site.js and revert the validator's shared-script existence check.

entries.evidence: The canonical GA4 reporting endpoint's optional Search Console query was incompatible, and two speculative GA4-query repairs were rolled back after Production-only validation failed. The isolated direct Search Console path was then blocked because Preview lacked the existing read-only Google credential. That credential path was safely made available to Preview, allowing the isolated direct endpoint to be functionally validated without altering GA4 collection or editorial authority.
entries.proposedChange: Use the isolated direct Search Console API read path for aggregate search-performance reporting instead of retrying incompatible GA4 Core Reporting dimension/metric combinations.
entries.expectedBenefit: Restore search-performance reporting without risking the healthy core GA4 feed or weakening credential boundaries.
validation: fresh feature branch was based on current main

Preview exposed only aggregate 7-day and 28-day Search Console metrics

no production runtime errors were present in the subsequent 24-hour check
entries.result: PR #136 merged and the direct Search Console endpoint is now validated in Production. The previous Search Console measurement blocker is cleared; core GA4 remains separate and healthy.
entries.rollback: Revert PR #136 to remove the direct Search Console endpoint; core GA4 collection and reporting are independent and should remain unchanged.

entries.evidence: automation/source-health.json was last fully checked on 2026-07-20 and records 28 URLs, including two temporarily unavailable sources. The ledger is now stale relative to the current newsroom cycle.
entries.proposedChange: Run a bounded source-health maintenance refresh against the existing registry and the primary sources used in the most recent Aug. 11-18 newsroom cycle; update statuses only from verified checks.
entries.expectedBenefit: Reduce stale-source and broken-link risk without adding work to the daily article publisher.
validation: recheck each existing source URL
verify current primary-source links used in the latest newsroom cycle
preserve temporarily unavailable versus removed/contradicted distinctions
entries.result: Pending the bounded Aug. 18 maintenance cycle; no source-health status is being inferred from age alone.
entries.rollback: Revert only any inaccurate source-health status changes; do not alter published reporting solely because a source is temporarily unavailable.

entries.evidence: The live Buffer metrics feed reports multiple tracked CUAI company-page posts as sent with exact item IDs, post IDs and sentAt timestamps, while their existing automation/social-queue.json records retained status: scheduled. The mismatch recurred across the tracked queue and could confuse handoff/reliability reporting even though delivery itself was healthy.
entries.proposedChange: Make the existing operating/reliability review reconcile an exact Buffer-sent item to the existing social-queue item in place, without creating a replacement post or calling the scheduler.
entries.expectedBenefit: Keep the internal social handoff ledger consistent with authoritative delivery evidence, eliminate repeated manual interpretation, and reduce false recovery/duplicate risk.
validation: new policy requires exact queue-item and postId match plus non-null Buffer sentAt
reconciliation is idempotent and preserves immutable UTM, schedule, post, channel and image fields
policy explicitly forbids scheduler calls, replacement items, destination changes, credentials or cadence changes
live Buffer metrics were re-read and exact sent evidence matched 12 tracked repository items
the Aug. 19 Treasury reservation remained scheduled and untouched
the legacy July 22 EricaAssist baseline remained untouched because it uses the legacy bufferPostId schema rather than the exact postId rule
entries.result: Reliability Watch reconciled 12 exact tracked Buffer-sent items in place to status sent and recorded Buffer sentAt/externalLink evidence. No scheduler call, replacement post, UTM change, destination change, cadence change or credential action occurred.
entries.rollback: Revert only the social-queue sent-state fields if any exact Buffer evidence is later shown to be mismatched; the external posts themselves are unchanged.
